# What's the Best Way to Keep the Records Needed for Credit Applications?


The best way is to maintain a continuously updated file for each farm, with property documents, production history, contracts, insurance, and financial data, so that a credit application can be assembled from existing records instead of a rush to find papers. On **Jestor** , this runs through **Docs** , linked **tables** , and a checklist for each application.


Lenders ask for many documents, and the farm may only learn which ones when it needs financing. Gathering them under time pressure delays decisions and may weaken the proposal.


## What scattered credit documents cost


- Delays in obtaining financing during planting windows
- Documents expired or missing when the lender asks
- Production history not available to support the request
- Repeated work for each new application
- Weaker negotiation because the farm looks disorganized


## How credit file management works


- A **file** for each farm holds documents with validity dates
- Production and financial data link to the same structure
- A checklist for each application shows what is missing
- Reminders prompt updates before documents expire


## Why Jestor fits this use case


- Applications can be prepared quickly
- Documents are current when they are needed
- Production history strengthens the proposal
- This scales from one farm to a group applying to several lenders


Documents gathered at the last minute A credit file kept ready


Delays and missing items Assembled quickly from current records


## Frequently Asked Questions


**Does Jestor decide or submit credit applications?** No, applications are submitted through the lender's channels; Jestor organizes the records. More at[jestor.com](https://www.jestor.com/?ref=blog.jestor.com) .


**Can I share a selected set of documents with a lender?** Yes, a restricted view or export can be prepared.


**Can I be reminded of expiring documents?** Yes, automation can alert you ahead of expiry.
